rationale: Real gaps: no default-step subquery, no direct tests for the new util/stats exports. Verified table contains no [x:] form.
Confirmed: stats is reassigned from the per-step-disabled run, so the PeakSamples-1 max check derives from an unasserted value.
tk is in subquery space (shifted by offsetMillis) but is compared to the unshifted ev.startTimestamp, skewing per-step attribution for offset subqueries.
Claims the doc links and anchors are fine, and they are. No actionable content.
Mutation-probe result reporting that the delta branch is pinned by tests; asserts no defect.
Checks schema/golden consistency and required-list handling and finds them correct.
Hypothesis of numSteps underflow raised and correctly refuted; truncating division keeps numSteps >= 1.
Enumeration confirming every IncrementSamplesAt* site has a paired read increment; accurate and non-actionable.
Boundary hypothesis raised and cleared: strict > is correct for the half-open window.
Bare mention of a double-registration hypothesis; the name is unique in the single MustRegister block, so nothing is asserted.
Correct readability point: with SamplesReadPerStep nil the timestamp argument is discarded, so the call mimics deliberate attribution it does not perform.
Accurate small coverage gap with a one-line fix; the disabled run in the test already reaches the branch.
Correct: the min-length guard is unreachable at the sole call site and untested. Coverage note on defensive code.
Confirmed asymmetry: sibling returns a non-nil empty map under the same conditions, and the doc comment states only one of two nil conditions.
Verifies that peak/max-samples behavior is untouched and finds it so; no defect claimed.
Four new exported helpers in a package downstream projects import ship with no direct tests; only IncrementSamplesReadAtTimestamp is exercised.
Confirmed: fullWindowCount is assigned only inside the recompute branch, so reused @-modifier steps now record 0 where the prior code recorded the retained window.
Correct: the new comment says only SamplesRead is merged, but UpdatePeakFromSubquery on the next line also merges the peak.
Hypothesis about the maxt-interval cutoff traced and cleared; claims correctness and is correct.
Real but small: embedders populating Statistics themselves emit samplesRead:0 with no unsupported signal. Same property as the pre-existing field.
The int conversion applies to the quotient, which is bounded by the outer step count, not to the millisecond numerator; no negative index is reachable on any word size.
Verified: no test case uses a default-step subquery, so noStepSubqueryIntervalFn feeding the new stats layout is untested for a common query form.
Flags the shipped IMPLEMENTATION NOTES scratch block and expectations recorded from output, the same point as the reviewer's 'shouldn't be here'.
A counter records contested semantics permanently into TSDB history; a real argument for settling the definition before shipping.
Panic hypothesis raised and refuted with correct arithmetic; asserts no defect.
Substantive: the quantity samplesRead measures is never defined, and evaluator-level counting cannot be storage reads. A maintainer must settle this.
Early-out hypothesis examined and correctly cleared; both counts are zero on that path.
Confirms the hoisted subqStart/Interval computation is value-identical to the prior inline code; no defect claimed.
Naming and registration checked and found conventional; no action.
Field alignment/ordering checked, no padding introduced, linter not enabled. Non-actionable.
Verified via git log: CHANGELOG.md is edited only at release cuts in this repo, so a per-PR entry is not the convention.
Confirms HPoint.size() is O(1); folded into another finding and asserts no defect itself.
Counter monotonicity checked and correct; explicitly not a finding.
Correct: the restore/merge is not deferred, so an ev.error panic skips it. Only affects queries that already fail.
Restates that the query log serializes the stats struct; no action for the reader.
Fair review point: the restructuring inflates the diff and drops the comment explaining the step-alignment computation.
Pre-existing observation raised and then explicitly set aside as out of reach; no actionable claim about this change.
The feature's core arithmetic has no direct unit test; covered only through a table entangled with subquery merging.
Confirmed real bug: currentSamples -= totalHPointSize(histograms) runs after truncation, subtracting retained rather than dropped size. Pre-existing.
Pre-existing pattern noted and dismissed as bounded and untouched.
The three attribution policies carry what-comments but no rationale; a human reviewer challenged exactly this attribution, so the gap is real.
Same substance as the reviewer disputing SamplesRead:2: the golden values encode the subquery double count instead of catching it.
Addresses the reviewer's question at the '// steps after last outer' comment: no subquery step exceeds subqEnd, so the clamp never fires and the comments are false.
Accurate naming point: the samples-read accessor returns a type named TotalSamplesPerStep in an exported package.
The HELP text of an existing metric is rewritten with a full-window claim that the fullWindowCount regression breaks; small but real.
Divergence hypothesis probed and found not live; recorded as latent, asserts no defect.
Negative-make hypothesis derived and refuted; claims safety and is correct.
Confirmed: countSamplesAfter scans the whole window per series per step, replacing an O(1) len(), and is gated by neither stats= nor the feature flag.
Pre-existing missing doc comment; mildly more confusing now that a sibling constructor propagates the parent setting.
Correct and small: the new, non-obvious SamplesRead numbers carry no derivation comments where TotalSamples does.
Checks whether the accessor is dead API and concludes it follows the existing test-accessor pattern; no action.
Actionable process point grounded in a real regression: a semantic change to an existing metric is buried inside an add-a-metric change.
Confirmed: totalSize is taken after extendFloats injects synthetic boundary points, so samplesRead counts points never read from storage.
Correct: the comment says 'subquery' inside the StepInvariantExpr case, which covers any step-invariant subtree.
Exponential-blowup hypothesis traced and correctly reduced to linear; folded into another finding.
Correct: InitStepTracking allocates TotalSamplesPerStep for the subquery child, which is written and then discarded unmerged.
Naming/help-text point: loaded vs read is not self-describing from the metric names alone.
Real asymmetry, functionally inert: StepInvariantExpr keeps NewChild() while the sibling case moved to NewChildWithStepTracking, undocumented.
Restates a cleared hypothesis about the empty-window continue; no defect.
Real: two numSteps-sized slices are now allocated per subquery, sized by query-controlled resolution, where NewChild allocated none. Gated on per-step stats.
Same point as the reviewer: GreaterOrEqual(SamplesRead, 0) holds for an unpopulated field, so the assertion checks nothing.
Aliasing hypothesis checked and cleared; the counts are computed before call().
Correct structural nit: the new ### section sits under the range-query heading although the instant-query section links to it.
Substantive: evalSeries charges a read per step per series, so a memoized stored sample returned at several steps is counted repeatedly under an I/O label.
States the nil receiver is guarded, which it is; no actionable content.
Enumerates the increment sites and confirms all are paired; a correct no-finding.
Correct but unreachable today: no guard on interval==0 or numSteps<=0, and the new call site widens the inputs reaching it.
Examines a claimed code/doc contradiction and concludes the code is correct; the residual doc wording is covered elsewhere.
Naming checked against the existing UpdatePeakFromSubquery vocabulary and found consistent; no action.
Accurate: the added nil guard is unreachable from either caller, unlike StepTrackingEnabled's which is load-bearing.
Correct observation: four near-duplicate increment helpers now apply three different bounds disciplines for the same job.
New unconditional per-step work in the innermost loop ships with no benchmark, and existing cases use windows too small to show it.
Double-count hypothesis on the reuse path checked and correctly cleared for the read axis.
Confirmed: the doc comment claims points in [mint,maxt] are retained while the drop loop makes the window half-open, and the new cutoff depends on that.
Concrete, actionable test proposal: a counting querier asserting samplesRead against real iterator yield would have caught the double count.
Correct API-shape asymmetry: a package-level constructor beside a method for the same child-from-parent role, forcing an extra exported accessor.
States the change adds no concurrency surface, which is true; nothing to act on.
Confirms the new counters are observational and do not touch the max-samples contract; no defect.
Explicitly declares a pre-existing size concern out of scope; no actionable content.
Fair: the accessor duplicates an exported field, its only value is the nil guard, and its name suggests initialization rather than the flag.
Real structural defect: the SubqueryExpr case reaches into another package's fields to implement a second merge instead of the helper written for it.
Off-by-one hypothesis raised and dismissed as intentional; asserts no defect.
Pre-existing vet notices on the base commit, explicitly excluded by the finder itself; unrelated to this change.
Mutation-probe bookkeeping showing the increment is pinned by tests; no defect claimed.
Cosmetic convention drift: bold field names where the surrounding file uses backticks.
Correct but contingent: a regression guard for an allocation bound that does not exist yet.
JSON member order is not significant and no golden pins it; the cluster says so itself.
Verified by grep: no test references the new counter, its registration, or its Add, so a missing MustRegister entry would fail silently.
Checks whether the scalar depends on the feature flag and correctly finds it invariant; no defect.
Grep confirms the built-in UI does not consume sample stats, so there is nothing to update.
Correct: the scalar increments while an out-of-range per-step write is silently dropped. Not reachable from current call sites.
Same substance as the reviewer's 'these tests seem very similar': byte-identical cases repeated two and three times.
Real: an always-present field in the stable v1 API freezes semantics that the review shows are still contested.
Declares that change rationale belongs in the PR description rather than code; no actionable finding.
The 'equals totalQueryableSamples for other query types' claim is false for step-invariant expressions and for subqueries, and is repeated in four places.
Accurate small consistency point: int64 return beside a sibling returning int, forcing an asymmetric cast at the call site.
Wording quibble about 'disk reads' in a comment; costs attention without changing anything.
Process note about the reviewer's own scratch artifact; not a property of the change.
Divide-by-zero hypothesis raised and correctly dismissed; Interval is non-zero whenever the arrays exist.
Confirmed in code: AggregateExpr returns preprocessExprHelper(n.Expr) only, so Param is never preprocessed. Real, pre-existing, unrelated to this change.
Allocation hypothesis checked and cleared; evalSubquery runs once per Call node.
Correct naming inconsistency: n where the sibling helpers name the same parameter samples.
Correct latent coupling: the formula mixes the evaluator's start with the stats object's interval, which the rewrite no longer guarantees to agree.
Real and undocumented: pre-window subquery steps collapse onto step 0 and trailing steps clamp to the last, systematically inflating the edge buckets.
Same point as the reviewer: the defaultEpsilon removal is unrelated churn that belongs in a separate change.
'when' versus 'if' in a doc comment; accurate and not worth a reader's attention.
Meta-commentary on a reviewer lane returning nothing; no claim about the code.
Same substance as the reviewer at query_stats.go:432: index-by-index merging assumes a 1:1 child/parent step mapping that nothing establishes.
Real doc/behavior mismatch: samplesRead and both counters are documented under the per-step-stats flag though only the PerStep arrays are gated.
Confirms no new sharing of QuerySamples; accurate and non-actionable.
Notes the deferred Add fires for failed queries and concludes it is correct and consistent with the sibling; explicitly not a finding.
Information-disclosure question examined and correctly cleared; the gating matches the existing field.
Concludes the helper's placement beside totalHPointSize is consistent; no action.
Strong, cheap test proposal: relational assertions (SamplesRead <= TotalSamples, sum of per-step) would catch misattribution that hand-listed goldens cannot.
Behavior-change hypothesis for the hoist checked and refuted; asserts no defect.
Correct wording inconsistency: the new description states flag gating that the identically gated sibling omits.
The 'unchanged semantics' comment is false given the reused-step regression it introduces, and it contradicts the surrounding docs.
Verified: smoothSeries has no samplesStats calls, so smoothed selectors report zero for both totals and the new read counter despite real storage reads.
Confirms registration and cardinality are fine; no defect claimed.
States both goldens were regenerated consistently, which they were; nothing to act on.
Double-registration and nil-stats hypotheses raised and dismissed correctly.
Correct doc-convention gap: the file marks new API surface with a version marker sixteen times; the new section has none.
Substantive release concern: a permanent counter and an always-emitted API field ship with no gate while the semantics are still being argued.
Ceiling division traced across cases and found correct; asserts no defect.
Nil-guard concern examined and cleared as consistent with the file's existing idiom.
Claims the zero read count on reused @ steps is intentional, which is correct; the defect is on the totals side and is reported separately.
Exactly the reviewer's point at engine_test.go:1551: the subquery's reads are merged and then the materialized matrix is counted again, giving 2 where 1 is right.
Confirms max-samples enforcement is untouched; correct and non-actionable.
Accurate small asymmetry in the new regexps; harmless given encoding/json output.
